absent: Validation rules for tracer option values and numeric width of option mask and shift.
Semantics of tracee memory access provider including forced flags and short result causes.
Acquisition behaviour and failure modes of signal hand stewardship and sighand lifetime.
Architecture single step and block step capability detection and enable or disable effects.
Construction of register set views and behaviour of provider retrieval and installation callbacks.
System call number argument return and architecture accessors and register context retrieval.
Seccomp filter storage ordinal resolution reference handling and metadata query behaviour.
Job control marking definitions and wakeup mechanics for traced and listening states.
Detach dispatch configuration compat conversion and FDPIC load map behaviours.
Numeric values sizes and binary layout of ABI request selectors flags and signal information.
Lifetime creation and clearing rules for retained trap information and retained message.

findings.text: Tracer bulk memory transfer interface moves a caller requested byte count between tracee address space and tracer user buffer with forced access, returning count moved and signalling access versus user copy failures distinctly.
Generic single machine word peek and poke interface for tracee memory with forced access, reporting access failure distinctly from user writeback failure.

Register set query interface locates a descriptor by core note identity and transfers a caller sized extent either outward to user memory or inward from user memory, enforcing size discipline and capacity limits.
Signal information export to user memory copies kernel representation then clears trailing expansion area, reporting user memory faults.

Central tracer request dispatcher selects behaviour by request selector covering memory peek and poke, options, event message, queued and current signal information, signal mask, interrupt and listen controls, detach, resume variants, termination, register sets, system call observation and mutation, seccomp queries, restartable sequence description and user dispatch configuration, with a default access failure for unsupported selections.
Bulk transfers use bounded staging and tolerate short provider results, returning progress made so far when later progress stalls while treating zero progress as access failure.
Option installation validates caller value then replaces only the dedicated option band within persistent tracer flags while preserving other bits, avoiding observable intermediate clearing.

Current trap signal details can be retrieved or replaced only when the tracee retains stored details. Absence yields invalid status and inability to secure signal hand stewardship yields search failure.
Queued signal inspection validates flags count and offset, chooses shared versus thread private queue by flag, and addresses entries by zero based skip count, stopping at end of queue.
System call observation always reports logical record extent for the active stop kind while transferring only the caller offered prefix, with common identity prefix plus kind specific payload.

System call mutation requires full record presence, rejects future control bits and stop kind changes, and enforces width preservation for numbers arguments and return values, with special handling that suppresses argument installation for the disabled number.
Register set transfer requires provider existence and caller length that is a multiple of element size, clamped to total descriptor capacity before dispatch by direction.

Register set retrieval clamps to descriptor capacity, materializes a zeroed staging area when caller supplies none, delegates production to provider callback, releases staging on provider failure, and reports bytes actually produced.
Resume validates requested signal number and, for stepped variants, requires architecture support, managing system call tracing and emulation markers according to requested resume kind.

Signal mask query and installation require exact mask extent. Query observes saved mask during restore deferral otherwise current mask, while installation unconditionally discards unblockable signals and clears restore deferral.
Restartable sequence description exposes user pointer value, extent length, signature and reserved flags, copying a truncated prefix when caller offers less while always reporting full extent.

Classic filter export is gated on administrator privilege and disabled caller enforcement mode, resolves filters by ordinal, probes total length when no destination is offered, and rejects filters lacking a preserved classic program with a medium type status.
Access to retained trap signal details occurs only under signal hand stewardship, released on all paths.
Walks of queued signals, publication of resume exit status with traced marker clearing and wakeup, and installation of blocked mask all occur under interrupt disabled signal lock stewardship.
Peek queue control block carries a flags word, a signed desired count and an offset. Only the shared queue selector bit is accepted.
Restartable sequence description layout comprises an address sized pointer value, a length, a signature and a flags word currently zero.

Observation record comprises operation discriminator, architecture identity, instruction and stack pointers, plus one active payload among entry number with arguments, exit value with error marker, or seccomp entry view with retained message.
Register set view is an array of descriptors each pairing core note identity with element count, element size and provider callbacks for retrieval and installation.
Pending signals are held as a linked collection of queued entries each embedding signal details. User visible signal information consists of kernel prefix followed by zeroed expansion slack.

Resume publishes caller supplied status, clears traced job control marking and wakes the tracee from traced sleep under lock, after selecting plain versus block versus single versus emulated single stepping behaviour.

Interrupt control requests a future stop trap without signal side effects and can cancel listening to force re trap, while listen control parks an already stopped tracee in listening state until asynchronous notification or interrupt re traps it.
Stop kind is derived from retained trap code and retained message, distinguishing system call entry and exit, seccomp stop, and absence of system call stop.

All user memory exchanges fail with fault status on inaccessible destinations or sources, with bulk and indexed transfers preserving already reported progress counts rather than converting them to errors.
Over wide offsets that exceed address width yield empty success rather than fault, and compatibility requesters receive converted signal information through a distinct narrow user path.
Extended queue scans yield execution voluntarily between entries and terminate early when the requesting context gains pending signal work.
ABI selectors include PTRACE_O_MASK placement handling plus PTRACE_PEEKSIGINFO_SHARED queue choice plus JOBCTL_TRACED lifecycle marking and JOBCTL_LISTENING lifecycle marking.

Observation discriminators include PTRACE_SYSCALL_INFO_NONE and PTRACE_SYSCALL_INFO_ENTRY plus PTRACE_SYSCALL_INFO_EXIT plus PTRACE_SYSCALL_INFO_SECCOMP alongside message tags PTRACE_EVENTMSG_SYSCALL_ENTRY and PTRACE_EVENTMSG_SYSCALL_EXIT.

Request vocabulary includes PTRACE_CONT and PTRACE_SYSCALL plus PTRACE_SINGLESTEP plus PTRACE_GETSIGINFO plus PTRACE_SETSIGINFO plus PTRACE_GETREGSET plus PTRACE_SETREGSET plus PTRACE_GET_SYSCALL_INFO plus PTRACE_SET_SYSCALL_INFO.
Negative statuses include EIO and EFAULT plus EINVAL plus ERANGE plus ESRCH plus EACCES plus EMEDIUMTYPE.
